summary.intent: Fix an excessively large release-please changelog on PR #427 (171 entries across 4 packages due to no prior release tags) and align the api-client package versions with the API version.
summary.outcome: Committed version alignment for @cipherbox/api-client and cipherbox-api-client (to 0.35.0), fixed hardcoded OpenAPI spec version by making it dynamic from npm_package_version, and configured release-please to auto-bump openapi.json on future releases. Bootstrap tags still need to be created and the release-please workflow re-run to actually fix PR #427.

repo: Release-please was introduced in phase 41 with no prior tags, causing it to treat the entire commit history as unreleased — fix is to create bootstrap tags at commit 7e7f4f458 for all 15 packages in the manifest.
The api-client packages (JS and Rust) are intended to be version-locked to the API (apps/api) — they should always share the same semver.
The OpenAPI spec version in packages/api-client/openapi.json was hardcoded at 0.1.0 and was never being updated, diverging silently from the actual API version.
Both apps/api/src/main.ts and apps/api/scripts/generate-openapi.ts independently hardcoded the OpenAPI version string — both needed fixing.

code.finding: OpenAPI DocumentBuilder version was hardcoded as '0.1.0'; changed to read from process.env.npm_package_version so it tracks the package version automatically.
Same hardcoded '0.1.0' version in the standalone OpenAPI generation script — also needed to be updated to use npm_package_version.

Added packages/api-client/openapi.json as an extra-file with a jsonpath expression ($.info.version) so release-please bumps the nested version field — a plain path only works for root-level version fields like package.json.

workflow: Running `cargo update` or `cargo generate-lockfile` pulls in unrelated upstream dependency updates; to update only specific workspace crates in Cargo.lock, use a targeted approach rather than full regeneration.

Release-please bootstrap: create tags named per the manifest conventions (e.g. @cipherbox/api-v0.35.0) at the last-known-good commit, push them, then re-run the workflow — the PR will regenerate with only post-tag commits.
For release-please extra-files, JSON files with nested version fields require jsonpath syntax (e.g. {"path": "openapi.json", "jsonpath": "$.info.version"}), not just a plain file path.

friction: Cargo.lock regeneration via cargo commands pulled in a large set of unrelated dependency updates, requiring a restore and more surgical approach.
OpenAPI version was silently stale at 0.1.0 across two source files and the generated artifact — discovered as a side effect of investigating the versioning work, not directly requested.
open_items: Bootstrap tags for all 15 packages (at commit 7e7f4f458) still need to be created and pushed — this is the actual fix for PR #427's bloated changelog.
After tags are pushed, the release-please GitHub Actions workflow needs to be manually re-run to regenerate PR #427 with a clean changelog.
Verify that npm_package_version is available in all environments where generate-openapi.ts runs (local dev, CI) so the version is never undefined in the generated spec.
